headline: Nationals rally past Phillies 10-4 in 11 innings
recap: Andrew Painter turned in a strong start, allowing one run on three hits with four strikeouts over four innings, but the Phillies' bullpen couldn't hold a 4-4 tie as Washington broke it open with a six-run 11th inning, beating Philadelphia 10-4 at Citizens Bank Park on Wednesday. Caleb Kilian recorded just one out while allowing five runs, four earned, and was tagged with the loss; Chase Shugart allowed an inherited run before finally ending the frame. CJ Abrams led Washington's offense, going 3-for-5 with three RBI, and Brady House added a solo home run. For Philadelphia, Luis Arraez hit a solo home run and Trea Turner, Bryson Stott and Justin Crawford each drove in a run.
The loss snapped the Phillies' winning streak. Philadelphia is 61-54, second in the NL East, 8.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves.

The Phillies continue their series with Washington tonight at Citizens Bank Park, first pitch 6:05 PM ET. Cristopher Sanchez starts for Philadelphia against Nationals right-hander Miles Mikolas. DraftKings has the Phillies as -332 moneyline favorites, -1.5 on the run line.
